<!-- question-type: inclass -->
### Exercise 8: Extending the request

So far, our function assumes that every request is for Australia.

**(a)** Suppose we also wanted the country to vary across requests. What would need to change in `get_indicator()`?

**(b)** We used `map()` when one input varied and `map2()` when two inputs varied. If year, indicator, and country all varied, what kind of change would we need to make to our mapping approach?

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-teaching-guide -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.teaching-block}

::: {.teaching-block-header}
Teaching Note
:::

::: {.teaching-block-body}

🎯 **Learning Objective**

Students should:

- recognise when another fixed part of an API request should become a function argument;
- generalise the progression from `map()` to `map2()` to cases where more than two inputs vary.

✅ **Core Concepts to Highlight**

- The country code is currently hard-coded as `"AUS"` inside `req_url_path_append()`.
- If country varies, it should become another argument of `get_indicator()`.
- `map()` is useful when one input varies.
- `map2()` is useful when two inputs vary together.
- When more than two inputs vary, `pmap()` provides the more general approach.

💬 **Suggested In-Class Prompts**

- Which line of `get_indicator()` currently fixes the country as Australia?
- What new argument would you add to the function?
- Why would `map2()` no longer be enough if three inputs changed across requests?

📌 **Common Misunderstandings**

- Thinking that only query parameters can become function arguments. Values in the URL path can vary as well.
- Looking for a `map3()` function rather than recognising `pmap()` as the generalisation.

:::

:::

:::

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-solutions -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-solutions" when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.solution-block}

::: {.solution-block-header}
Solution
:::

::: {.solution-block-body}

(a)

The country code is currently fixed as `"AUS"` inside `req_url_path_append()`.

To allow the country to vary, we would add a `country` argument to `get_indicator()` and replace `"AUS"` with `country` inside the path.

(b)

We would need a mapping approach that can work across more than two changing inputs.

In `purrr`, we can use `pmap()` when we want to pass several inputs to the same function.

:::

:::

:::
